per_claim.note: With RB-GS15 and bilinear prolongation, the Poisson solve reached tolerance in 5 cycles across 33x33..513x513 grids (rho≈0.0089), and the paper’s piecewise-constant restriction also converged in 6 cycles (depth≥3).
On Poisson, deep V-cycles (V3–V7) reached tolerance in 5–6 cycles from a flat guess, but the BU8 640x64 case (~37 iterations) was not tested.

V1 stagnated (~2e-6 reduction after 50 sweeps) while V2 needed 21 cycles and V3–V7 only 5–6 cycles to reach tolerance, indicating orders-of-magnitude speedup though O(10^5) iterations were not measured.
Convergence improved from depth 2 (21 cycles) to depths 3–7 (5–6 cycles) and then saturated, in both node-centred and cell-centred tests.
Measured orders were 2.04 (L1), 2.02 (L2), and 2.0006 (Linf) with pairwise rates ~2.00, confirming second-order accuracy.
The FAS nonlinear solve for −Δu+u^3 achieved residuals ~5.8e-10 with depth≥2 and consistent errors (~1.85e-5) from a flat guess, but did not hit the 1e-10 tolerance or the paper’s xCFC system.

Using full-weighting (node-centred) yielded 5-cycle convergence, while the paper’s piecewise-constant restriction (cell-centred) also reached ≤1e-11 residual in 6 cycles for depth≥3, preserving the qualitative convergence.

judgement.justification: The replication strongly confirms the multigrid convergence mechanism: grid-independent convergence with RB-GS smoothing, rapid deep V-cycle performance, saturation of rates with depth, verified second-order spatial accuracy, and successful use of the paper’s piecewise-constant restriction stencil; it also demonstrates FAS on a canonical nonlinear problem. However, the full scope of the paper—xCFC nonlinear Einstein solves on a spherical grid, the complete GRHD stack with reconstruction and Riemann solver, and BU8 mode-frequency recovery—was not reproduced, and the specific BU8 iteration counts and the full xCFC nonlinear tolerance behavior were not directly tested, warranting a PARTIAL verdict.
